statements.text: The label attribute is not applied as an accessible name; assistive technology reads the option's content. Keep label matching the visible text.
A disabled option, or any option in a disabled violet-option-group, gets aria-disabled and is skipped by arrow keys and type-ahead and cannot be chosen.

events.description: Emitted when the option is chosen, for the list that owns it.
events.name: request-select

slots.description: Trailing content such as a shortcut or count.
slots.name: after

slots.description: Leading content such as an icon.
slots.name: before

summary: One choice inside a violet-select, violet-combobox or violet-listbox; it does nothing on its own.

usage.text: The value attribute defaults to the option's text when omitted. Selection is matched by value, so every option under one parent needs a distinct value.
The label attribute replaces the option's text for the select trigger, the combobox input, filtering and type-ahead; the slotted content still renders. Text in named slots never counts as the label.
The default slot is the label; the before slot takes leading content such as an icon, after takes trailing content such as a count, and description takes a second line of text.
A click asks the parent select, combobox or listbox to choose it; the parent consumes that request. Listen for change on the parent, not on the option.
Inside a combobox, do not set hidden on options yourself: the combobox overwrites every option's hidden attribute while filtering.
